title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The top of the page closes the 'cas particulier' from the previous page. There A is perfect (one may take A = F_p), so Ã = A and B̃ = B. When B is reduced, B̃ → Λ is an isomorphism, and the Cartier operation becomes a map C: Z*(B) → Ω*_B with C(f^p ω) = f C(ω), C(x^{p-1}dx) = dx and C(dx/x) = dx/x. Grothendieck notes that this is the situation of Cartier's original text (1957).

Section (4), 'Fonctorialité, Globalisation', globalises the local algebra construction to a morphism X → S in characteristic p.
- Set-up: X^{(p/S)} = X ×_{S,F_S} S. The absolute Frobenius F_X factors through the relative Frobenius f = F_{X/S}: X → X^{(p/S)}, which is radicial and surjective. (The label 'f = f_{X/S}' sits ambiguously next to the vertical arrow X^{(p/S)} → S, but the subsequent use of f_*(O_X) shows f is meant to be the relative Frobenius.)
- Inverse Cartier map: Grothendieck defines a homomorphism of sheaves of graded algebras ψ: Ω*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} → f_*(Z*(Ω*_{X/S})). It sends a ⊗ λ to a^p λ and d(x ⊗ 1) to x^{p-1}dx. Composing with Z* → H*, and using that f is affine so f_* commutes with cohomology, gives ψ: Ω*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} → H*(f_*Ω*_{X/S}) ≅ f_*H*(Ω*_{X/S}).
- Factoring through Λ: let Λ = Im(O_{X^{(p/S)}} → f_*O_X) = O_{X^{(p/S)}}/J. The kernel J is a nilideal: the absolute Frobenius of X^{(p/S)} factors through f, so a ∈ J implies a^p = 0. The target is a Λ-module through H^0, so ψ factors through ψ̃: Ω*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} ⊗_{O_{X^{(p/S)}}} Λ → H*(f_*Ω*_{X/S}). The remark Ω^1 = 0 refers to Ω^1_{Λ/O_{X^{(p/S)}}} = 0. If X^{(p/S)} is reduced, Λ is simply O_{X^{(p/S)}}; his example of when this holds is only partly legible.
- Cartier isomorphism: if f_*O_X locally admits a p-basis over O_{X^{(p/S)}}, the algebraic results of the previous pages show ψ̃ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the global Cartier isomorphism C̃: H*(f_*Ω*_{X/S}) → Ω*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} ⊗ Λ. Precomposing with Z* → H* gives the Cartier operation C̃: Z*(f_*Ω*_{X/S}) → Ω*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} ⊗ Λ.
- Margin note: define C̃ directly once ψ is known to be an isomorphism, without passing through p-bases. This is an axiomatic standpoint: Cartier exists wherever the inverse Cartier map is an iso.
- The next page adds base-change functoriality, then begins (5): connections on invertible sheaves, logarithmic forms, and p-curvature (compatibility with p-th powers).
errors: The label f = f_{X/S} is placed next to the vertical arrow X^{(p/S)} → S, while f is then used as the relative Frobenius X → X^{(p/S)}. This is a notational slip.

The parenthetical claim that X^{(p/S)} is reduced, e.g. when X is locally of finite presentation over S, is partly illegible. As a general statement it is false: X reduced does not imply X^{(p/S)} reduced. Some hypothesis on S (e.g. perfect or reduced plus smoothness) is needed.
The factorisation through Λ needs no reducedness: ψ is O_{X^{(p/S)}}-linear and the target is a Λ-module. The detour through Ω^1 of Λ is unnecessary but harmless.

ideas.what: Relative inverse Cartier map ψ: Ω*_{X^{(p)}/S} → F_*H*(Ω*_{X/S}) as a homomorphism of graded algebras, and its inverse C, globalised over a base S of characteristic p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier (1957) for the absolute case; Katz (1970, Nilpotent connections, §7) and Deligne–Illusie (1987) for the relative version
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA as such; the topic of these notes was later taken up by Katz.

ideas.what: Cartier isomorphism under the hypothesis that O_X locally has a p-basis over O_{X^{(p/S)}} (weaker than smoothness), with correction by Λ = image of O_{X^{(p)}} in F_*O_X when X^{(p)} is not reduced
ideas.modern_name: Cartier isomorphism for morphisms with p-bases
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz 1970; Berthelot (crystalline cohomology, 1974) uses p-bases; Kato for the log/p-basis setting

ideas.what: Characterisation C(x^{p-1}dx) = dx, C(dx/x) = dx/x, C(f^p ω) = f C(ω) in the perfect-base case
Defining C as the inverse of ψ wherever ψ is an iso, independently of p-bases (margin note)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kato (Cartier smooth algebras, 1986); later Bhatt–Lurie–Mathew on Cartier smoothness

missed.claim: The margin proposes taking 'ψ is an isomorphism' as the defining hypothesis for the Cartier operation, bypassing p-bases. This anticipates the later notion of Cartier-smooth algebras (Kato), which reappears in recent work on de Rham–Witt complexes and the de Rham comparison. Here it is only a programmatic remark.
missed.quote: définir C̃ directement une fois que ψ est un iso (sans parler avant … des p-bases …)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically it shows Grothendieck isolating the 'Cartier isomorphism holds' condition around 1972, before Kato. It is of historical interest only, since the notion is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard globalisation of the Cartier isomorphism in the relative setting with p-bases, which Katz published around 1970. The only mildly notable features are the careful handling of a non-reduced X^{(p/S)} via Λ, and the margin idea of defining C wherever ψ is an iso, an early hint of 'Cartier smoothness'.
transcription_corrections: 'C'est le cas envisagé dans le texte initial de Cartier' — the reading 'envisagé' is plausible.
In the diagram, the curved arrow on top is F_X: X → X, and the lower arrow is F_S: S → S. The vertical arrow X^{(p/S)} → S is the one labelled f = f_{X/S}, though f is used as the relative Frobenius.
The struck-out box reads approximately: 'Supposons que f_*(O_X) soit localement une p-base … Im(O_{X^{(p/S)}} → f_*(O_X)), alors on trouve un homomorphisme de faisceaux d'Algèbres'.
The first ψ target is f_*(Z*(Ω*_{X/S})), and the next line is 'd'où un homomorphisme ψ: Ω*_{X^{(p/S)}/S} → f_*(H*(Ω*_{X/S})) ≃ H*(f_*(Ω*_{X/S}))'.

'Si Λ = Im(O_{X^{(p/S)}} → f_*(O_X))' is followed by a bracket: '[qui est de la forme O_{X^{(p/S)}}/J, J un nilidéal, donc Ω^1_{Λ/…} = 0; si S réduit et X loc. de présentation finie … si X^{(p/S)} est réduit, p.ex. …]'. Exact wording uncertain.
In the margin, 'avant' may be 'au préalable'. Content: define C̃ directly once ψ is an iso, without p-bases.
